Interested individuals without this license should visit the links below for more information regarding the alternative licensure process. (All licenses require the candidate to have earned at least a Bachelor's Degree.)Residency Model License Pathways (from dpi.nc.gov)List of Approved Educator Preparation Programs (from dpi.nc.gov)----------------------------------------------------------------------------------MAJOR FUNCTION: Management of Instructional Time The teacher has materials, supplies, and equipment for each lesson ready at the start of the lesson or instructional activity; gets the class started quickly; gets students on task quickly at the beginning of each lesson; maintains a high level of student time-on-task. MAJOR FUNCTION: Management of Student Behavior The teacher has established a set of rules and procedures that govern the handling of routine administrative matters; has established a set of rules and procedures that govern student verbal participation and talk during different types of activities—whole-class instruction, small group instruction, etc.; has established a set of rules and procedures that govern student movement in the classroom during different types of instructional and non-instructional activities; frequently monitors the behavior of all students during whole-class, small group, and seat work activities and during transitions between instructional activities; stops inappropriate behavior promptly and consistently, yet maintains the dignity of the student. MAJOR FUNCTION: Instructional Presentation The teacher begins lesson or instructional activity with a review of previous materials; introduces the lesson or instructional activity and specific learning objectives when appropriate; speaks fluently and precisely; presents the lesson or instructional activity using concepts and language understandable to the students; provides relevant examples and demonstrations to illustrate concepts and skills; assigns tasks that students handle with a high rate of success; asks appropriate levels of questions that students handle with a high rate of success; conducts lesson or instructional activity at a brisk pace, slowing presentations when necessary for student understanding but avoiding slowdowns; makes transitions between lessons and between instructional activities within lessons efficiently and smoothly; makes sure that the assignment is clear; summarizes the main point(s) of the lesson at the end of the lesson or instructional activity. MAJOR FUNCTION: Instructional Monitoring of Student PerformanceThe teacher maintains clear, firm and reasonable work standards and due dates; circulates during class work to check all students’ performance; routinely uses oral, written, and other work products to check student progress; poses questions clearly and one at a time. MAJOR FUNCTION: Instructional FeedbackThe teacher provides feedback on the correctness or incorrectness of in-class work to encourage student growth; regularly provides prompt feedback on assigned out-of-class work; affirms a correct oral response appropriately, and moves on; provides sustaining feedback after an incorrect response or no response by probing, repeating the question, giving a clue, or allowing more time. MAJOR FUNCTION: Facilitating InstructionThe teacher has an instructional plan which is compatible with the school and system-wide curricular goals; uses diagnostic information obtained from tests and other assessment procedures to develop and revise objectives and/or tasks; maintains accurate records to document student performance; has instructional plan that matches/aligns objectives, learning strategies, assessment and student needs at the appropriate level of difficulty; uses available human and material resources to support the instructional program. MAJOR FUNCTION: Interacting Within the Educational EnvironmentThe teacher treats all students in a fair and equitable manner; interacts effectively with students, co-workers, parents, and community. MAJOR FUNCTION: Performing Non-Instructional DutiesThe teacher carries out non-instructional duties as assigned and/or as need is perceived; adheres to established laws, policies, rules, and regulations; follows a plan for professional development and demonstrates evidence of growth. Performs other related work as required.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------Please direct any specific licensure or employment questions to hr@martin.k12.nc.us.

jobs.description: Employer: Pittsburgh Public Schools Expires: 11/04/2026 POSITION TITLEBuilding SubstituteJOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARYThe Building Substitute is directly supervised by School Principals, Assistant Principals or Department Leads and supported by the Office of Human Resources. This position is assigned to one school for the 192-day school year (including Professional Development and Clerical Days). This position is responsible for delivering instruction using provided lesson plans or appropriate substitute activities when plans are not available, while maintaining a safe, structured, and supportive learning environment that aligns with district and school-wide expectations. Building substitutes are expected to work anywhere they are needed, including teacher, counselor, social worker, librarian, or paraprofessional absences, as well as lunch duty, playground monitor, or other duties assigned by school administration.This role requires flexibility in working across various grade levels and assignments, as well as the ability to quickly adapt to changing environments. The Building Substitute is expected to support the district’s mission by fostering a positive, inclusive learning environment and demonstrating cultural competence while working with diverse student populations. All required paperwork and documentation must be completed and submitted within fourteen (14) calendar days of receipt to ensure timely processing.Once all materials have been received and reviewed, Human Resources will complete the final approval process and notify the applicant of their hiring status and eligibility to begin accepting substitute assignments.Building Substitute Assignment:In April, school leaders recommend substitute professionals to serve as Building Substitutes for the following school year. Once recommendations are received, offers are sent to candidates who will have 5 business days to accept or decline.After all offers are finalized, a survey will open for any remaining Building Substitute positions. All substitute professionals can apply for these openings through June. The survey will close on the last day of school for students.If you are hired as a substitute professional between June and March and are interested in becoming a Building Substitute, please email subservices@pghschools.org. You will receive a list of available positions and should reply with your top three choices. Assignments will be made based on school needs. WORK MONTHS10 monthsESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS1. Monitor assignments in Frontline and accurately track and maintain time in accordance with district procedures, working with the school secretary as needed to ensure records are accurate.2. Support students in completing assigned work by providing help, guidance, and redirection as needed.6. Actively engage with students throughout the school day and during instruction by providing support and encouraging participation in activities.7. Monitor students across various school settings, including classrooms, hallways, cafeterias, assemblies, and other school activities, to ensure safety and appropriate behavior.8. Work cooperatively with teachers, paraprofessionals, and other school staff to support a positive and inclusive learning environment.9. Other relevant duties as assigned by supervisor in support of the department's or school’s goals and objectives and the District's mission and Superintendent's Priority GoalsEDUCATION REQUIRED· Requirements visit the a href="https://www.education.pa.gov/Educators/Certification/PAEducators/Pages/PACerts.aspx">PA Department of Education’s Certification Types and Codes webpage.YEARS OF EXPERIENCEN/AKNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES· Demonstrated ability to work with children in an educational setting preferred· Be flexible and adapt to different classrooms, student needs, and daily assignments.· Strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills· Commitment to professionalism, reliability, and punctuality· Ability to quickly adapt to new environments and responsibilities· Demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, effectively managing multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.· Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess situations, identify solutions, and effectively manage responsibilities· Proven ability to build, foster, and sustain strong, professional relationships with school leaders, staff, parents, and students to support a positive and productive school environment.· Ability to handle sensitive information with a high degree of confidentiality, while consistently demonstrating professionalism, sound judgment, discretion, tact, and diplomacy in all interactions.· Demonstrated cultural competence and the ability to work district.· Value, demonstrate, and promote diversity, equity, and inclusion.WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTSThe working conditions and physical requirements described here are representative DiscoverBefore building, you will listen.You will research:Youth demographics and community needsEducational institutions and universitiesExisting youth-serving organizationsService gaps and unmet needsWorkforce and career opportunitiesFunding and philanthropy opportunitiesCommunity organizations and trusted leadersPotential university chapters and partnershipsKey Deliverable:A credible San Francisco Community Needs Assessment and Local Strategic Plan. 2. ScoutYou will help determine what a Youth RISE presence should look like in San Francisco.This includes:Identifying potential office locationsExploring shared and partner spacesEvaluating program and meeting facilitiesConsidering transportation and accessibilityIdentifying university proximity and collaboration opportunitiesAssessing operational needs and costsWe believe the goal is not to build the largest footprint.The goal is to build the right footprint. 3. BuildYou will build the local organization.This includes:Community relationshipsStrategic partnershipsVolunteer recruitmentStaff recruitmentUniversity relationshipsCommunity visibilityLocal systemsPrograms designed around actual community needsA sustainable annual operating planYou will help establish the culture, credibility, relationships, and systems that future generations of Youth RISE leaders will inherit. 4. FundA mission requires resources.The Founding Executive Director will work closely with Youth RISE national leadership and shared-services functions to help develop a sustainable local funding strategy.This may include:Foundation grantsCorporate partnershipsSponsorshipsGovernment opportunitiesIndividual donorsMajor giftsCommunity fundraisingIn-kind partnershipsYou will not be expected to build funding infrastructure alone.However, you will be expected to lead the local effort and build meaningful relationships that support the long-term sustainability of the San Francisco office. 5. OperateOnce the office launches, you will be responsible for ensuring it functions effectively.This includes leadership and accountability for:Staff leadershipProgram implementationCommunity relationshipsBudget managementOffice operationsRisk managementCompliancePerformance reportingOrganizational cultureStrategic executionA successful office should eventually be capable of operating through systems and leadership—not solely through one person. 6. ServeAbove everything else, this role exists to serve young people.The Founding Executive Director should consistently ask:"Does this help us create greater opportunity for the young people we serve?"If the answer is no, we reconsider the decision.This is not a role built around titles.It is a role built around impact. What Success Looks LikeWithin the First 90 DaysYou will be expected to work toward:A written community needs assessmentA local strategic planA partnership pipelineA funding pipelineIdentified priority partnersA preliminary office and infrastructure strategyA clear launch planWithin the First 6 MonthsThe San Francisco office should be progressing toward:Operational readinessEstablished partnershipsApproved programmingInitial fundingCommunity engagementLaunch preparation and/or program deliveryWithin the First 9 MonthsThe office should be working toward:A functioning local teamActive partnershipsProgram deliverySustainable operating systemsNational reporting and accountabilityBy the 12-Month ReviewSuccess will be evaluated through areas including:Community impactPartnershipsProgram effectivenessFunding developmentTeam developmentOrganizational cultureOperationsCommunity reputationMeasurable outcomes for young people Who We Are Looking ForWe are looking for a builder.Someone who can walk into a community, listen before speaking, identify opportunities, and bring people together around meaningful work.You may come from:Nonprofit leadershipYouth developmentHigher educationGovernmentCommunity organizingWorkforce developmentPhilanthropySocial servicesHealthcareEducationPublic affairsBusinessEntrepreneurshipCommunity developmentWe are less interested in whether your résumé follows a traditional path than whether you can demonstrate:LeadershipPeople have trusted you to lead difficult and meaningful work.JudgmentYou can make thoughtful decisions, even when information is incomplete.CompassionYou treat people with dignity and respect.ExecutionYou have actually built things—not simply talked about building them.IntegrityYou handle responsibility, relationships, resources, and mistakes with honesty.ResilienceYou understand that meaningful work is difficult, and you know how to continue moving forward. Experience We ValueWe welcome candidates with experience working alongside communities and populations that may include:Young people experiencing homelessnessFoster and former foster youthLGBTQIA+ youth and communitiesImmigrant and newcomer communitiesFirst-generation college studentsYoung people experiencing educational barriersYoung people experiencing economic instabilityJustice-impacted individualsUnderserved communitiesCommunities historically excluded from opportunityYouth RISE evaluates candidates based on their experience, qualifications, leadership capability, and ability to perform the role. The Ideal Candidate Can Answer:What have you built that still exists today?How have you earned trust in a community?When were you wrong about what a community needed, and what did you do next?What meaningful partnership have you built from the ground up?What funding relationship have you helped develop?How have you helped change the trajectory of a young person or community?How do you turn vision into execution?How do you build something that can continue beyond you? Reporting StructureThe Founding Executive Director is part of the Youth RISE Foundation national leadership structure.The Founding Executive Director will work closely with and receive support from the national executive office, including functions responsible for:OperationsFinanceHuman ResourcesProgramsLearning & DevelopmentPublic AffairsExecutive LeadershipThe San Francisco office remains part of one national organization and operates within the Foundation's established governance, financial, programmatic, compliance, and organizational standards. What Youth RISE ProvidesYouth RISE Foundation provides the national framework, mission, vision, organizational standards, and infrastructure to support founding leaders.You will have access to:National executive leadershipOrganizational guidanceEstablished policies and standardsProgram frameworksHuman Resources infrastructureCompliance and screening processesFinancial controls and supportProfessional developmentNational shared servicesCross-city collaborationA national network of founding leadersYou will not be expected to build alone.But you will be expected to lead. This Role Is for You If...You see a problem and immediately begin thinking about how to solve it.You believe young people deserve access to more opportunity.You know how to build relationships across different communities and sectors.You can speak with a university leader, corporate executive, community organizer, donor, and young person—and treat every person with the same dignity.You understand that leadership is not about being the most important person in the room.It is about making the room better because you were there.You are comfortable with ambiguity.You are not waiting for a perfect system before beginning meaningful work.You want the opportunity to build something that may outlast your own tenure. This Is Not a Traditional Executive RoleWe want to be transparent.A founding opportunity requires a different kind of leader.This is not an established office with:A large existing staffA mature local donor baseLongstanding community relationshipsFully developed local programsAn established office infrastructureYou will be helping create those things.That means there will be difficult days.There will be unanswered emails.There will be partnerships that do not work out.There will be funding opportunities that do not materialize.There will be problems nobody anticipated.That is what founding means.You are there to help solve problems that do not have answers yet. Equal OpportunityYouth RISE Foundation is committed to building an inclusive organization and considers qualified candidates based on relevant experience, demonstrated capability, and the requirements of the position.The Foundation is committed to fair and equitable recruitment practices and does not require candidates to disclose personal history or membership in any community as a condition of consideration. jobs.title: AmeriCorps Math Fellow - Small Group Instruction at Blueprint Schools Network
jobs.description: Employer: Blueprint Schools Network Expires: 11/04/2026 ​ AmeriCorps Math FellowOrganization: Blueprint Schools NetworkProgram: AmeriCorps Math Fellows ProgramTerm of Service: One Academic School Year Position Location(s): Balsz School District - Phoenix, ArizonaAbout Blueprint Schools Network & The RoleAt Blueprint Schools Network, we believe that every student possesses incredible potential that deserves to be fully realized through high-quality, personalized instruction. As an AmeriCorps Math Fellow, you won’t just support students—you’ll help expand access to high-quality math instruction for young people who deserve every opportunity to succeed. Along the way, you’ll build the skills, experience, and confidence to become an exceptional educator and community leader.As a Fellow, you will deliver intensive, small-group math instruction during the school day, working directly with students to build their confidence, strengthen their foundational math skills, and help them reach their full potential. You will receive structured onboarding, regular 1-on-1 coaching, collaborative lesson planning, and whole-group professional development throughout the program year.This is practice-based learning at its best: you grow as an educator in real time, backed by a supportive professional network.Real service. Real students. Real results.Why This Role MattersThe opportunity gap is real—and Fellows help close it.Far too many students—disproportionately those from historically under-resourced communities—move through school without receiving the rigorous, personalized math support they need to build lasting confidence and academic momentum. The effects compound: students who fall behind early are less likely to access advanced coursework, post-secondary opportunities, and economic mobility.Blueprint Math Fellows serve at exactly this inflection point. By providing daily, intensive small-group instruction, Fellows accelerate learning, rebuild academic confidence, and help students access the full promise of their education. The impact isn't abstract—it is measurable, and it belongs to you.Term Options & National Service BenefitsAmeriCorps service comes with a bi-weekly living allowance rather than a salary or hourly wage over the term of service (academic school year). Within each region, the final living allowance falls within a specific band determined by the local school/program day schedule and average daily on-site service hours.Living stipend band ranges (for school day schedules of 6 hours or more) per region for 2026-2027 School Year are:• Arizona: $21,000 to $24,000* prorated based on start date. *Living Stipend: Living allowances are paid out in equal bi-weekly installments across the active term of service. Total stipend amounts may be adjusted for members starting after the official program launch date based on remaining pay periods. In addition to the living stipend, Blueprint AmeriCorps Math Fellows that meet AmeriCorps service hour requirements and remain in good standing are eligible for an end-of-term living allowance balance aligned with their AmeriCorps slot.• Three-Quarter Time (1,200 service hours): $1,000• Half-Time (900 service hours): $500Note: The majority of service hours are completed through direct tutoring services provided to students during the school day. Remaining service hours are earned through professional development and volunteer activities.**End-of-Term Living Allowance Balance: End-of-term living allowance balance disbursement upon completing all required service hours while remaining in good standing. Full details regarding Blueprint’s living stipend and End of Year Completion Bonus are provided to candidates during the recruitment process. Additional Member Benefits• Eli Segal AmeriCorps Education Award: Upon successful completion of your term, members may earn an Education Award usable toward existing qualified student loans or future higher education tuition and expenses.Segal AmeriCorps Education Award Amounts (subject to start date and completion of service hours)Full-Time - service hours required 1,700 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $7,395.00Three-Quarter Time - service hours required 1,200 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $5,176.50Half-Time - service hours required 900 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $3,697.50Reduced Half-Time - service hours required 675 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $2,817.14Quarter-Time - service hours required 450 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $1,956.35Note: An individual may earn up to the value of two full-time education awards in their lifetime across all national service terms. Under current federal law, the Segal Education Award is considered taxable income in the calendar year in which it is used/redeemed. • Healthcare Coverage: Full-time members are provided medical, dental, and vision with 100% of the individual-level premium paid by Blueprint. Cost-sharing plans are available to add dependents. • SNAP Benefits: AmeriCorps members are eligible to apply for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits to help offset monthly food costs through their state programs. Eligibility is determined by individual state rules.• Loan Forbearance & Interest Accrual Repayment: Eligible federal student loans may be placed in forbearance during service, with interest paid off by AmeriCorps upon successful term completion.• Built-in Professional Time: Paid time designated specifically for daily prep/planning and up to 72 hours of professional growth and 1-on-1 instructional coaching.Blueprint Schools Network BenefitsOur Benefits & Employee Well-being• Planning and Preparation: Daily planning and preparation built into your schedule• 30 minute duty free lunch• Sick leave and personal leave• One-on-One coaching and ongoing feedback.• Real-world experience valued across education and mission-driven careers • Fellows enrolled in Blueprint’s medical plan have access to All One Health Assistance Program: Access confidential, 24/7/365 support at no cost to you or your household members. Services include professional mental health counseling, financial and legal and work-life. Phone, app, or portal.• Ongoing Well-being Support: Take advantage of monthly interactive EAP orientation sessions designed to help you navigate and maximize your mental health, financial, legal, and work-life benefits. • Telehealth & Virtual Care: Access board-certified primary care doctors, dermatologists, and behavioral health therapists via video or phone through MDLIVE and Talkspace. • Pre-Tax Commuter Savings: Save up to 30% on public transit, parking, and vanpooling expenses with convenient payroll deduction accounts. Key Responsibilities (AmeriCorps Member Service Activities)During your term of service, you will:• Deliver High-Impact Instruction: Lead daily, small-group math instruction during the school day for small cohorts of students.• Data-Driven Support: Track student progress and adapt instructional approaches in real time using assessment data.• Build Meaningful Relationships: Foster strong, trusting relationships with students to build academic confidence, engagement, and a positive mindset toward math.• Collaborate with Educators: Partner closely with classroom teachers, school administrators, and fellow AmeriCorps members to align tutoring with classroom instruction.• Engage in Professional Growth: Participate in daily planning sessions, 1-on-1 coaching, and structured professional development (up to 72 hours per year).• Maintain Service Commitments: Complete required service hours over the course of the school year.From Tutor to Teacher: Explore Your PathwayWhether you are exploring a career in teaching, planning to get certified, or simply driven to do meaningful work, the Math Fellow role gives you the foundation to move forward with purpose.Through our "Tutor to Teacher" path, you will gain essential professional skills like communication, adaptability, and problem-solving. As you consider your next steps, Blueprint connects Fellows with partner organizations and pathways into teaching, formal teacher certification, and graduate study.Qualifications & Eligibility RequirementsAmeriCorps Eligibility Requirements:• Be at least 18 years of age at the start of service.• Be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or lawful permanent resident.• Satisfy the National Service Criminal History Check requirements.Role Qualifications:• Education: Current enrollment in a degree program, prior enrollment, or completion of an Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree.• Language Skills: Proficiency in English required; Spanish language skills are a plus.• Core Competencies: Passion for educational equity, strong communication skills, empathy, adaptability, and a desire to work directly with students.• Commitment: Ability to commit to the full school-year term of service and reliably commute to assigned school placement and commit to assigned schedule.• Satisfy Blueprint and local school/district background screening requirementsApply TodayThis is more than a role—it’s a chance to build a career rooted in purpose, impact, and growth.Apply today and start making a difference.This program is available to all, without discrimination on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy, religion, age, national origin, genetic information, disability, military status, familial status, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by law. Blueprint Schools Network is an equal opportunity organization committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion.This material is based upon work supported by AmeriCorps under Grant No. 26NDFMA001. Program services are funded in part by AmeriCorps and local matching public funds. ​

jobs.title: Elementary Literacy Tutor Contractor (Crossroads Academy - Quality Hill and Central Street)) at Crossroads Charter Schools
jobs.description: Employer: Crossroads Charter Schools Expires: 11/04/2026 Job Description: Literacy Tutor - Part-time Contractor Direct Supervisor: Principal or designee School Summary:At Crossroads Charter Schools, we… Understand the significant difference between equity and equality. Every student deserves to receive what he/she needs to succeed (equity), not that every student receives the same amount of resources, instruction, attention, etc. (equality).Develop school environments where all students are actively and meaningfully engaged in rigorous instruction and authentic learning tasks.Interrupt the “school to prison pipeline” – policies and practices that are directly and indirectly pushing the most at risk students out of school and on a pathway to the juvenile and criminal justice systems.Engage families as partners in meaningful ways.Build the capacity of diverse teams that are more reflective of our students.Nurture an open, collaborative, and trusting environment because the work is enormous, deeply personal, emotional and often difficult. Engage in on-going job embedded professional development through co-teaching and co-planning Position Summary: We are seeking dedicated and passionate Literacy Tutors to join our team and provide reading support to students in small groups. The Literacy Tutor will work closely with students to enhance their literacy skills, focusing on key aspects of the Science of Reading, a research-based approach to reading instruction. This is a part-time position that provides the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on students' academic success.Position Responsibilities: Provide individualized and small-group instruction to students, focusing on literacy skills such as reading comprehension, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, and fluency.Utilize evidence-based practices informed by the Science of Reading to tailor lessons that meet the diverse needs of students.Implement various instructional strategies to foster students' reading development and confidence.Assess student progress regularly through informal and formal assessments, adjusting instruction as necessary to ensure continued growth.Collaborate with classroom teachers and other educational staff to align tutoring support with the school's literacy goals.Maintain a positive, engaging, and supportive learning environment to encourage student participation and progress.Provide feedback and reports on student progress to teachers and parents when necessary.Demonstrate gains in student performanceParticipate in meetings, training and professional developmentMeet professional obligations through efficient work habits such as: meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, coordinating, etc.Act in a professional and ethical manner at all times and comply with school policies, procedures, and expectations.Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by their supervisor. Skills and Qualifications:Understanding of/willing to learn about literacy development, reading strategies, and the Science of Reading principles Experience working with students on reading and literacy, preferredExcellent communication skills and the ability to build rapport with students from diverse backgrounds.Patience, adaptability, and a passion for helping students succeed.A degree/training in education, literacy studies, or a related field, preferredDesire to continue professional developmentExcellent organization skills and an ability to coordinate multiple tasks and activitiesOutstanding verbal and written communication skills and an ability to keep multiple stakeholder groups, including parents, teachers, staff, volunteers and partners, informed of critical issues, activities and schedules. An ability and enthusiasm for promoting the school and its mission to a broad and diverse group of people.Excellent work ethic, positive attitude, flexibility and willingness to perform tasks assignedDemonstrates ethical behavior and confidentiality of information about students and teachers in school environment and community.Must pass background check PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. This job requires that the employee be able to: sit, stand, walk, speak, hear, use hands, fingers, reach with hands and fingers; bend, stoop, lift objects of at least ten pounds. Job requires the employee occasionally to stoop, kneel, crouch. Visual ability requires mono and color vision, close vision, distance vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud and is a standard acceptable level for this environment. Is directly responsible for students’ safety, work output and well-being. jobs.title: Behavior Technician - Denver at Horizons ABA
jobs.description: Employer: Horizons ABA Expires: 11/04/2026 Job descriptionMONTHLY BONUSES AND MULTIPLE ANNUAL RAISES FOR TOP PERFORMERS. APPLY TO FIND OUT MORE!Pay Range: $20-$28 per hourExpected Hours: 20-30 hours per weekClient Locations: Colorado: Aurora, Brighton, Broomfield, Centennial, Denver, Lakewood, Littleton, Longmont, Parker, ThorntonClients Availability: Weekdays - Daytime, Afternoons & Evenings. Weekends - Anytime (optional).BenefitsQuarterly financial bonuses for hitting targetsMileage reimbursementWellness programs and retreats, regular social events and team outingsReferral program and bonusesOpportunities for professional development, continuing education and internal promotions.Continuing Education support and library accessAdditional Benefits for Full-Time RBTS:Comprehensive health insurance packages.PTO – 10 DaysPaid Family LeavePaid Sick Time401kAbout the Job OpportunityWe are seeking dedicated Behavior Technicians (BTs) and Registered Behavior Technicians (RBTs) to join the growing Horizons ABA team! The BT or RBT will work directly under the supervision of a BCBA (Board Certified Behavior Analyst) to provide high-quality ABA therapy (Applied Behavior Analysis) to children with autism and other developmental disabilities. The ideal candidate will have a genuine passion for working with children and a strong interest in behavioral therapy. We hire BTs and RBTs with the intention that our hires will transition into more senior roles at Horizons, including full time and leadership RBT roles, BCBA roles ultimately Clinical Director and managerial roles.Why Work with Us?We started Horizons ABA because we wanted to build an ABA company with a unique, therapist-centric culture; together with our clinical leadership we have created an environment that is growth-oriented, professional, and fulfilling. Here is how:I. Compensation: We believe our team deserves to be compensated well for their efforts, contributions, and achievements. We offer competitive compensation and benefits and a variety of regular bonuses based on achievable milestones. We want you to hit them!II. Training and Career Development: We offer comprehensive training and mentorship opportunities for our RBTs. Whether our RBTs are interested in full time technician leadership positions or in pursuing a masters degree and a BCBA role, we support them. From financial stipends to specialized training programs, Horizons will help you reach your career goals. Join us and start building a rewarding career!III. Leadership and Engagement: Our clinical leadership is world-class and provides direct guidance and mentorship to our RBTs. In addition, the two founders are mission-driven and intimately involved in day-to-day operations and work with all of our staff directly. At our company everyone has a voice and if you have feedback or suggestions, we want to hear about it!IV. Work / Life Balance: At Horizons, we believe in work-life balance and we help our RBTs find the right balance of Scheduling that best suits their interests, availability, and needs. From current in-home opportunities where we strive to minimize our team’s commutes to upcoming clinic-based roles in 2025, we work with you to find the perfect balance for you!V. Reduced Administrative Burden: We utilize innovative software, AI tools, and efficient workflows to reduce our RBTs’ tedious administrative work and provide them with more time to focus on their clinical passions and build their behavioral therapy skills.VI. Our Culture: We diligently built our company from scratch to create an inviting and therapist-centric culture. We lead with empathy. Character, ethics, and attitude are as important to us as intellect, ambition and work ethic. Making sure our team members feel supported and heard is core to our identity. We foster community through exciting team outings and social events. We want you to enjoy being a part of our team!Key Responsibilities IncludeDirect TherapyImplement individualized ABA treatment plans developed by BCBAs.Provide 1:1 therapy sessions to clients in settings including homes, schools, and community locations.Utilize ABA techniques such as discrete trial training, natural environment teaching, and behavior modification strategies.Data Collection and ReportingAccurately collect and record data on client behavior and progress during each session.Maintain detailed session notes and progress reports.Communicate client progress and any concerns to the supervising BCBA.Client and Family InteractionBuild positive and supportive relationships with clients and their families.Assist in training parents and caregivers to implement ABA strategies in the home.Provide guidance and support to families to help generalize skills learned in therapy.Collaboration and TeamworkParticipate in team meetings and supervision sessions with BCBAs.Collaborate with other RBTs and therapists to ensure consistent implementation of treatment plans.Contribute to a positive and productive team environment.QualificationsHigh school diploma or equivalent; Bachelor’s in Psychology, Education, or related field preferred.Current certification as an RBT or willingness to obtain RBT certification.Experience working with individuals with ASD or other developmental disabilities is preferred.Experience working with children is a big plus.Strong understanding of or interest in behavioral therapy principles and technique.Excellent communication and interpersonal skillsAbility to follow detailed treatment plans and instructions.Valid driver's license and reliable transportation (if applicable).And most importantly – kindness, integrity, empathy and a genuine desire to help others.WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR WHEN WE HIREOur team is what makes our company stand out in an industry with many different types of providers. We understand that it takes a special type of person to succeed in this role, and we are committed to only hiring the best of the best clinicians to foster a high-quality, collaborative environment. Horizons ABA is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.Apply now to become part of an exceptional team transforming lives through ABA Therapy!

jobs.title: Intensive Home-Based Clinician II (IHBC) at Blue Kite Wellness
jobs.description: Employer: Blue Kite Wellness Expires: 11/04/2026 Intensive Home-Based Clinician II (IHBC)Sign-On Bonus!Location: Pontiac, IL and surrounding areasWork Setting: Field-based hybrid — services provided in clients’ homes and communities, with telehealth when permittedHelp Children and Families Create Meaningful, Lasting ChangeBlue Kite Wellness provides accessible, compassionate, individualized, and holistic mental health services to children, teens, adults, and families. We are seeking an Intensive Home-Based Clinician (IHBC) to support children, youth, and families participating in the Illinois Pathways to Success program.The IHBC provides individualized, short-term behavioral health services in the settings where children and families live and grow. This role develops assessment-informed intervention plans, provides therapeutic services focused on symptom reduction and improved family functioning, and offers clinical direction to Intensive Home-Based Support (IHBS) staff.The clinician works collaboratively with youth, caregivers, Care Coordinators, Child and Family Team members, and other authorized providers. Services are strengths-based, family-centered, solution-focused, and informed by Managing and Adapting Practice (MAP) and other HFS-approved approaches.What You’ll DoProvide Intensive Home-Based Clinical services to eligible children, youth, and families in accordance with authorized service plans and Illinois Pathways requirements.Use the youth’s IM+CANS, Functional Behavioral Assessment, clinical observations, family input, and Child and Family Team recommendations to develop and adjust individualized clinical interventions.Deliver individual, family, caregiver, and cross-system therapeutic interventions that support symptom reduction, emotional and behavioral functioning, family stability, and the youth’s ability to remain safely at home and in the community.Strengthen caregiver capacity, family communication, problem-solving, coping, emotional regulation, and behavioral-management skills.Provide clinical direction and consultation to assigned IHBS staff, including communicating intervention goals, reviewing progress, and modifying strategies when clinically appropriate.Participate as an active member of the Child and Family Team and collaborate with caregivers, Care Coordinators, schools, crisis-response providers, and other authorized supports.Support crisis prevention, safety planning, de-escalation, and post-crisis follow-up within the clinician’s scope of practice.Monitor client progress, identify emerging needs or safety concerns, and recommend appropriate changes to services and clinical plans.Complete timely, accurate, objective, and clinically appropriate documentation in accordance with Blue Kite Wellness, payer, and Illinois HFS requirements.Participate in supervision, case consultation, team meetings, required training, and continuing professional development.What We’re Looking ForRequired QualificationsMeets current Illinois requirements for a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) or Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA), including all applicable education, licensure, supervision, credentialing, and scope-of-practice requirements.Master’s degree in social work, counseling, psychology, or a related behavioral health field from an accredited institution.At least two years of progressively responsible behavioral health experience, including substantial experience working with children, adolescents, and families.Strong clinical assessment, engagement, treatment-planning, family-intervention, crisis-prevention, de-escalation, documentation, and care-coordination skills.Ability to work independently in home and community settings while collaborating effectively with a multidisciplinary team.Sound clinical judgment, professional boundaries, adaptability, and effective communication skills.Reliable transportation, a current valid driver’s license, and current auto liability insurance for travel to client homes and community locations.Experience with complex behavioral health needs, family systems, crisis intervention, intensive or community-based services, Functional Behavioral Assessments, and evidence-informed clinical practice is strongly preferred.Work Setting and ScheduleThis is a field-based position involving frequent local travel and independent work in clients’ homes, schools when authorized, community locations, and office settings. Telehealth may be used when permitted by the service plan and program requirements.Scheduling is based on youth and family needs and may include evening hours. Clinicians must be able to safely navigate varied home and community environments and respond professionally during stressful or emotionally charged situations. The role also requires appropriate availability and responsiveness consistent with IHB program expectations, including scheduled support outside traditional business hours when needed including evenings and one weekend day. Compensation and Work StructureSalaried: $55,000–$65,000 annuallySign-On Bonus: This position is eligible for a $2,000 sign-on bonus, paid in two installments: $1,000 after six months of employment and $1,000 after one year of employment.Placement within the applicable compensation range is based on experience, licensure, credentials, and overall qualifications. Reimbursable mileage is paid at the current IRS standard mileage rate.BenefitsDepending on position classification and eligibility, Blue Kite Wellness offers:Medical and dental insurancePaid time offPaid holidaysProfessional-development stipendEmployee referral programMileage reimbursement for eligible business travelWhy Join Blue Kite Wellness?Meaningful work: Make a direct difference for children and families in your community.Professional growth: Receive ongoing training, supervision, and opportunities to develop your clinical skills.Supportive culture: Join a collaborative and inclusive team that values compassion, accountability, flexibility, and respect.Administrative support: Our administrative team manages referrals, client onboarding, billing, and insurance so clinicians can remain focused on care and outcomes.Equal Employment OpportunityBlue Kite Wellness is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that values diversity and supports the unique contributions of all employees.Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)Blue Kite Wellness may use AI-powered tools to support administrative and operational functions, such as drafting job postings, developing training materials, and preparing internal communications. AI tools are not used to make hiring or employment decisions. All employment decisions are made by qualified personnel in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

jobs.title: Community Engagement Intern at Starlight
jobs.description: Employer: Starlight Expires: 11/04/2026 Position Description: This internship will take place entirely in person at the Starlight Theatre campus. The Community Engagement Intern will work closely with full-time community engagement staff members while focusing on planning, preparation and implementation of programming throughout the summer, including the Community Tickets program, Bob Rohlf Internships, Just Imagine, Performances for Young Audiences, Arts Bridge, and other initiatives. The intern will often work directly with program participants (students, parents, guardians, and community members) and will lead collaborative projects with other members of the Bob Rohlf Internship program. The school opened in 2004, added grades 7 - 12 in 2015 and 2016. Teachers are highly involved in developing curriculum and writing materials, as well as decision making at the school. In fact, the school's board of directors has a teacher majority. Occasional travel is required.Grants to Teachers: The LILA Foundation frequently offers "Inquiry 360" grants to teachers to pursue enriching experiences that they can bring back to share in the classroom. Teachers are encouraged to pursue these experiences abroad. Inquiry 360 grants are competitive and are awarded in April for use the following summer.Social Functions: We usually start the school year with an all staff gathering in August, and have a January staff party with guests as well. Each Friday, various staff members offer well-attended gatherings around sports or exercise, including volleyball, football (soccer), kettlebells, or Zumba. Other social activities abound. Our staff works hard, and has a lot of fun in the process!

jobs.title: Part-Time After-School Entrepreneurship Lead Coach at Kidfoundry
jobs.description: Employer: Kidfoundry Expires: 11/04/2026 After-School Program Entrepreneurship Primary Coach —Employer: KidFoundry LLC Location: Multiple Public Schools Houston, Texas — on-site Position type: Part-time, school-term position Student group: Grades 2–5 Schedule: Typically 2-4 Days of the week, approximately 3:00–4:30 p.m Program dates: 01/05/2027- 05/28/2027* ( Can be selected for the next term based on performance)Compensation: $25–$40 per hour based on experience and expertise. Reports to: KidFoundry Program Director About KidFoundry KidFoundry helps children develop an entrepreneurial mindset through hands-on projects, games, teamwork, and presentations. Our elementary-age programs introduce students to identifying problems, developing product ideas, creating prototypes, understanding customers, setting prices, marketing, and pitching. Along the way, students practice creativity, communication, problem-solving, and collaboration. Our goal is to help children turn their ideas into something they can explain, develop, and share with confidence. About the role We are seeking a dependable, engaging instructor to deliver KidFoundry’s existing entrepreneurship curriculum as an after-school program at multiple elementary schools around Houston. This opportunity is well suited to a candidate who enjoys working with children and has an interest in business, education, entrepreneurship, or youth development. Selected candidates will be given priority for various holiday camp positions- summer, spring, thanksgiving and winter. You will lead interactive lessons and guide students through projects using KidFoundry’s lesson plans and activities. You will also manage classroom routines, supervise students, and help create a welcoming and fun environment where children feel comfortable asking questions, trying ideas, and learning from mistakes. KidFoundry will provide curriculum training, lesson plans, program materials, and ongoing guidance. You are not expected to design a new curriculum. What you will do ● Review the provided lesson plan before each session and prepare the materials needed. ● Arrive in time to set up the classroom and receive students according to the school’s procedures. ● Teach entrepreneurship concepts through short explanations, relatable examples, games, and hands-on activities. ● Guide students as they brainstorm ideas, build prototypes, explore pricing and marketing, and prepare simple pitches. ● Facilitate teamwork, discussions, and presentations so every student has opportunities to participate. ● Establish clear routines and use calm, positive strategies to address distractions, disagreements, and transitions. ● Adapt explanations and provide support for students with different ages, abilities, and confidence levels while maintaining the lesson’s learning goals. ● Maintain accurate attendance and supervise students throughout the session and authorized dismissal. ● Follow school and KidFoundry procedures for safety, emergencies, student privacy, and professional conduct. ● Organize supplies, clean up the learning space, and provide a brief session update to the Program Director. ● Communicate promptly about supply needs, student concerns, incidents, or scheduling problems. ● Weekly camp briefing to the Camp Director in person or remote. Required qualifications ● Direct experience working with children through camp counseling, tutoring, coaching, classroom assistance, after-school programs, or structured youth volunteering. ● Ability to lead activities, explain instructions clearly, and maintain a respectful, organized learning environment. ● Interest in entrepreneurship and willingness to learn and accurately deliver KidFoundry’s curriculum. ● Strong communication, organization, and follow-through. ● Consistent availability for the advertised schedule and commitment for the full program session. ● Reliable transportation to and from the schools ● Willingness to complete required background screening, school clearance, and program training before working with students. Experience gained through volunteering is welcome. Please describe the children’s ages, your responsibilities, and whether you led groups independently. Preferred qualifications ● Current enrollment in a college or university program/ or a graduate degree, particularly business, entrepreneurship, marketing, education, psychology, communications, or a related field. ● Experience leading groups of elementary-age children. ● Familiarity with positive classroom management and hands-on learning. ● Coursework or practical experience involving product development, marketing, budgeting, or presentations. ● Current CPR/first-aid certification. What we provide ● Paid curriculum training and onboarding. ● Ready-to-use lesson plans, activities, and program materials. ● Ongoing support and feedback from KidFoundry’s leadership. ● Practical experience in teaching, facilitation, youth development, and entrepreneurship education. ● A consistent after-school schedule. How to apply Submit your résumé and a short statement to hr@Kidfoundry.com explaining: 1. Why are you interested in the program coach position at KidFoundry. 2. Your experience working with children, including their ages and any group leadership responsibilities. 3. Your availability during the program dates. 4. Two Professional references and permission to contact them. Please also include two professional references and permission to contact them. For student applicants, references may include a teacher, professor, volunteer coordinator, or supervisor familiar with your reliability and work. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and then a brief teaching demonstration using a prompt supplied by KidFoundry. If selected, paid training will be held during Thanksgiving break 23rd November- 27th November 2026* in person during our camp. Application deadline: 30th October 2026 KidFoundry welcomes applicants from different academic backgrounds who can bring patience, creativity, reliability, and a commitment to helping children learn. * dates are subject to change

jobs.title: (#ENTRY015603) Entry Level – Work with Children at Fraser
jobs.description: Employer: Fraser Expires: 11/04/2026 Build Something Bigger — And Change Lives, Including Your Own. In 1935, Louise Whitbeck Fraser opened a school in her home for people with disabilities — defying social expectations and choosing compassion over convention. She believed everyone deserves the chance to reach their potential and thrive. Today, that same bold spirit is alive in every Fraser service. We’re still building something bigger — a more inclusive, connected world where everyone belongs. At Fraser, you’ll find more than a job. You’ll find purpose. You’ll find growth. And you’ll find a place where your work changes lives — including your own.Fraser is looking for passionate, dedicated individuals to join our team and make a lasting impact on children with autism spectrum disorder and other developmental needs. Whether you're new to the field or bring years of experience, this is a role where you can truly make a difference and grow both personally and professionally.Why Join Us?Competitive Pay: The starting pay range for this role is $18.00 to $21.63 hourly depending upon experience and education.Paid Training & Supervision: We cover your RBT certification process, plus ongoing training to support your career growth.No Experience Needed: If you’re new to this field, we offer comprehensive training at full pay, including the first two weeks dedicated to getting you up to speed.Flexible Hours: Monday through Friday schedule with no nights or weekends.Career Advancement: We offer continuous training, tuition discounts, career path opportunities, transparent feedback, and promotion opportunities.Employee benefits: Free snacks at all sites! Student loan repayment contributions, and more.Benefits for Full-time Employees (30+ hours per week):Medical, dental and vision insuranceHealth Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA)Employee Assistance Plan (EAP)Life, AD&D and Voluntary Life InsuranceLong-Term Disability, Accident Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance and Hospital Indemnity InsurancePet Insurance403(b) Retirement Plan with Company MatchWork-Life Balance; 5 weeks of paid time off annually (18 days PTO + 9 Paid Holidays) Opportunities for community involvement in Fraser-organized eventsCareer growth opportunitiesEmployee Referral BonusesResponsibilities:Work 1:1 with children aged 2 to 7 years old in a clinical or center-based environment, applying evidence-based Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) techniques.Implement and track progress on therapeutic goals, collect data, and engage in fun activities that help children develop essential skills (e.g., social awareness, communication, self-care, safety).Foster a positive and engaging environment with children through play, movement, singing, reading, and more!Communicate effectively with team members, families, and supervisors to share progress and feedback.Help maintain a clean, safe, and stimulating therapy space.Qualifications:Education: High school diploma or GED required. A bachelor’s degree in psychology, Sociology, Child Development, or a related field is preferred.Experience: Previous experience in childcare, mental health, or as a paraprofessional is a plus, but not required.Passion: A love for working with children, particularly those with autism spectrum disorder and other developmental challenges.Other: Reliable transportation, ability to pass a background check, and a commitment to diversity and inclusion.Hiring at Available Locations:St. Cloud, MN Encouraged to Apply: Paraprofessional, Certified Nursing Assistant, Special Education Teacher, Personal Care Assistant, Direct Support Professional, Direct Support Professional, Home Health Aide, Mental Health Practitioner, Childcare Provider, Caregiver, Social Worker, Behavioral Technician, ABA Therapist, Applied Behavior Analysis Therapist, Behavior Therapist, Mental Health Practitioner, Mental Health Worker, Behavioral health TechniciansWhy Join Fraser?Meaningful ImpactHelp individuals and families lead more connected, independent, and fulfilling lives. Your impact here is real — and lasting.Competitive Pay & BenefitsFraser offers fair pay and comprehensive benefits that support your health, well-being, and future goals.Flexibility & Work-Life Balance With flexible schedules, generous paid time off, and wellness programs, Fraser helps you care for others without sacrificing yourself.Grow Your Career With UsWe invest in your development with training, licensure support, leadership pathways, and real opportunities to advance.Culture That Lives Its ValuesInclusion isn’t just a buzzword — it’s how we operate. You’ll be seen, heard, and supported to bring your full self to work.Thrive with Stability and PurposeWith nearly 90 years of trusted service and continued growth, Fraser is a nonprofit where you can build a lasting, mission-driven career.Fraser is Minnesota’s leader in autism, mental health, and disability services — and one of the few Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) in the state. As a nonprofit organization, we provide integrated community behavioral healthcare that improves quality, accessibility, and coordination of care. We lead with compassion, innovate with purpose, and fight for inclusion — every single day. Ready to Build Something Bigger? Join Fraser. Grow with us. Make a difference. Because when you thrive, so does the world around you.Fraser is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.This position will be posted at https://www.fraser.org/jobs until filled. You must apply online here to be formally considered.If you are having trouble applying or have questions, please contact Fraser HR at careers@fraser.org or 612.767.7550. If you have successfully submitted your application, you will get a confirmation email. If you do not receive the confirmation email, please check your junk/spam folders, then contact us as we may not have received your application. Thank you for considering Fraser!

jobs.title: Therapeutic Mentor at Blue Kite Wellness
jobs.description: Employer: Blue Kite Wellness Expires: 11/04/2026 Therapeutic Mentor Location: Stone Park, Bellwood, Melrose Park, Westchester, IL Work Setting: Field-based hybrid — In-home, community-based, and telehealth sessionsHelp Children and Families Create Meaningful, Lasting ChangeBlue Kite Wellness provides accessible, compassionate, individualized, and holistic mental health services to children, teens, adults, and families. We are seeking a Therapeutic Mentor (TM) to support children and youth participating in the Illinois Pathways to Success program.The Therapeutic Mentor provides individualized, strengths-based services in clients’ homes and communities. In the Therapeutic Mentor role, the employee works one-on-one with youth to strengthen communication, confidence, emotional regulation, interpersonal skills, problem-solving, and positive social behaviors. The Therapeutic Mentor works collaboratively with youth, Care Coordinators, Child and Family Team members, and other authorized providers to support coordinated, family-driven, and youth-guided care. What You’ll DoProvide Therapeutic Mentoring services to eligible youth in accordance with authorized service plans and Illinois Pathways requirements.Work one-on-one with youth to practice and strengthen communication, emotional regulation, problem-solving, self-advocacy, confidence, interpersonal skills, and positive social behaviors.Collaborate with the Child and Family Team, the Pathways Supervisor, the supervising QMHP or LPHA, and other authorized providers.Recognize changes in youth's engagement, behavior, service needs, or safety and promptly communicate concerns to the appropriate supervisor or clinical team member.Complete timely and accurate documentation and participate in supervision, coaching, case consultation, team meetings, and required training.Maintain a reliable schedule, communicate changes promptly, and follow Blue Kite Wellness procedures related to confidentiality, professional boundaries, client safety, mandated reporting, and crisis response.What We’re Looking ForRequired QualificationsHigh school diploma or equivalent.At least 21 years of age.At least one year of experience working with children, adolescents, families, behavioral health needs, skill building, mentoring, or community-based services preferred.Ability to build rapport with youth and caregivers, model positive behavior, and teach practical skills.Strong communication, organization, documentation, and collaboration skills.Ability to work independently in home and community settings while accepting and applying supervision, coaching, and feedback.Willingness and ability to complete the Illinois Pathways Therapeutic Mentor training process, Blue Kite Wellness orientation, and all required ongoing training and coaching.Reliable transportation, a current valid driver’s license, and current auto liability insurance for travel to client homes and community-based service locations.Preferred QualificationsAdditional education in psychology, social work, counseling, education, human services, or a related field.Familiarity with behavioral health, education, healthcare, child welfare, juvenile justice, or other child- and family-serving systems.Work Setting and ScheduleThis is a field-based position involving frequent local travel and independent work in clients’ homes, schools when authorized, community locations, and office settings. Telehealth may be used when permitted by the service plan and program requirements.Scheduling is based on youth and family needs and may include evening hours. Must be able to safely navigate varied home and community environments and respond professionally during stressful or emotionally charged situations. The role also requires appropriate availability and responsiveness, including scheduled support outside traditional business hours when needed including evenings and one weekend day.Compensation and Work StructureHourly direct client care: $30.00–$35.00 per hourHourly indirect and administrative work: $17.05 per hourDirect client care includes individual and family therapeutic services and applicable caregiver or team collaboration. Indirect and administrative work may include documentation, travel between client locations, care coordination, clinical supervision, required meetings, training, and professional-development activities. Hourly employees are paid based on actual hours worked.Placement within the applicable compensation range is based on experience, licensure, credentials, and overall qualifications. Reimbursable mileage is paid at the current IRS standard mileage rate.BenefitsDepending on position classification and eligibility, Blue Kite Wellness offers:Medical and dental insurancePaid time offPaid holidaysProfessional-development stipendEmployee referral programMileage reimbursement for eligible business travelWhy Join Blue Kite Wellness?Meaningful work: Make a direct difference for children and families in your community.Professional growth: Receive ongoing training, supervision, and opportunities to develop your clinical skills.Supportive culture: Join a collaborative and inclusive team that values compassion, accountability, flexibility, and respect.Administrative support: Our administrative team manages referrals, client onboarding, billing, and insurance so clinicians and mentors can remain focused on care and outcomes.Equal Employment OpportunityBlue Kite Wellness is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that values diversity and supports the unique contributions of all employees.Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)Blue Kite Wellness may use AI-powered tools to support administrative and operational functions, such as drafting job postings, developing training materials, and preparing internal communications. AI tools are not used to make hiring or employment decisions. All employment decisions are made by qualified personnel in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

jobs.title: Intensive Home-Based Clinician II (IHBC) at Blue Kite Wellness
jobs.description: Employer: Blue Kite Wellness Expires: 11/04/2026 Intensive Home-Based Clinician II (IHBC)Sign-On Bonus!Location: Waukegan, IL and surrounding areasWork Setting: Field-based hybrid — services provided in clients’ homes and communities, with telehealth when permittedHelp Children and Families Create Meaningful, Lasting ChangeBlue Kite Wellness provides accessible, compassionate, individualized, and holistic mental health services to children, teens, adults, and families. We are seeking an Intensive Home-Based Clinician (IHBC) to support children, youth, and families participating in the Illinois Pathways to Success program.The IHBC provides individualized, short-term behavioral health services in the settings where children and families live and grow. This role develops assessment-informed intervention plans, provides therapeutic services focused on symptom reduction and improved family functioning, and offers clinical direction to Intensive Home-Based Support (IHBS) staff.The clinician works collaboratively with youth, caregivers, Care Coordinators, Child and Family Team members, and other authorized providers. Services are strengths-based, family-centered, solution-focused, and informed by Managing and Adapting Practice (MAP) and other HFS-approved approaches.What You’ll DoProvide Intensive Home-Based Clinical services to eligible children, youth, and families in accordance with authorized service plans and Illinois Pathways requirements.Use the youth’s IM+CANS, Functional Behavioral Assessment, clinical observations, family input, and Child and Family Team recommendations to develop and adjust individualized clinical interventions.Deliver individual, family, caregiver, and cross-system therapeutic interventions that support symptom reduction, emotional and behavioral functioning, family stability, and the youth’s ability to remain safely at home and in the community.Strengthen caregiver capacity, family communication, problem-solving, coping, emotional regulation, and behavioral-management skills.Provide clinical direction and consultation to assigned IHBS staff, including communicating intervention goals, reviewing progress, and modifying strategies when clinically appropriate.Participate as an active member of the Child and Family Team and collaborate with caregivers, Care Coordinators, schools, crisis-response providers, and other authorized supports.Support crisis prevention, safety planning, de-escalation, and post-crisis follow-up within the clinician’s scope of practice.Monitor client progress, identify emerging needs or safety concerns, and recommend appropriate changes to services and clinical plans.Complete timely, accurate, objective, and clinically appropriate documentation in accordance with Blue Kite Wellness, payer, and Illinois HFS requirements.Participate in supervision, case consultation, team meetings, required training, and continuing professional development.What We’re Looking ForRequired QualificationsMeets current Illinois requirements for a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) or Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA), including all applicable education, licensure, supervision, credentialing, and scope-of-practice requirements.Master’s degree in social work, counseling, psychology, or a related behavioral health field from an accredited institution.At least two years of progressively responsible behavioral health experience, including substantial experience working with children, adolescents, and families.Strong clinical assessment, engagement, treatment-planning, family-intervention, crisis-prevention, de-escalation, documentation, and care-coordination skills.Ability to work independently in home and community settings while collaborating effectively with a multidisciplinary team.Sound clinical judgment, professional boundaries, adaptability, and effective communication skills.Reliable transportation, a current valid driver’s license, and current auto liability insurance for travel to client homes and community locations.Experience with complex behavioral health needs, family systems, crisis intervention, intensive or community-based services, Functional Behavioral Assessments, and evidence-informed clinical practice is strongly preferred.Bilingual in Spanish and English.Work Setting and ScheduleThis is a field-based position involving frequent local travel and independent work in clients’ homes, schools when authorized, community locations, and office settings. Telehealth may be used when permitted by the service plan and program requirements.Scheduling is based on youth and family needs and may include evening hours. Clinicians must be able to safely navigate varied home and community environments and respond professionally during stressful or emotionally charged situations. The role also requires appropriate availability and responsiveness consistent with IHB program expectations, including scheduled support outside traditional business hours when needed including evenings and one weekend day. Compensation and Work StructureSalaried: $55,000–$65,000 annuallySign-On Bonus: This position is eligible for a $2,000 sign-on bonus, paid in two installments: $1,000 after six months of employment and $1,000 after one year of employment.Placement within the applicable compensation range is based on experience, licensure, credentials, and overall qualifications. Reimbursable mileage is paid at the current IRS standard mileage rate.BenefitsDepending on position classification and eligibility, Blue Kite Wellness offers:Medical and dental insurancePaid time offPaid holidaysProfessional-development stipendEmployee referral programMileage reimbursement for eligible business travelWhy Join Blue Kite Wellness?Meaningful work: Make a direct difference for children and families in your community.Professional growth: Receive ongoing training, supervision, and opportunities to develop your clinical skills.Supportive culture: Join a collaborative and inclusive team that values compassion, accountability, flexibility, and respect.Administrative support: Our administrative team manages referrals, client onboarding, billing, and insurance so clinicians can remain focused on care and outcomes.Equal Employment OpportunityBlue Kite Wellness is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that values diversity and supports the unique contributions of all employees.Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)Blue Kite Wellness may use AI-powered tools to support administrative and operational functions, such as drafting job postings, developing training materials, and preparing internal communications. AI tools are not used to make hiring or employment decisions. All employment decisions are made by qualified personnel in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.
